title: Expand-and-sparsify gas classification vs SVMs on transient mixtures
setting: Synthetic 8-sensor gas array with first-order transients (random previous-stimulus initial state, gain jitter, noise) for 3 single gases and their 3 binary mixtures (6 classes), with a tunable saturating/interactive mixture nonlinearity. Methods classify the raw flattened transient: a LinearSVC, a CV-tuned RBF SVM, or a fixed random sparse binary expansion (D=2000, k-WTA 5%) with a one-pass binary Hebbian readout (potentiation probability chosen by hold-out). The metric is accuracy on held-out mixture transients (6-way decision).

paper.title: Online gas classification at the edge
paper.claim: A binary-weight Hebbian expand-and-sparsify network outperforms a linear SVM on gas mixtures and roughly matches an optimised non-linear SVM.

metric.name: mixture_acc
metric.description: Fraction of held-out mixture-class transients (300 fresh samples) classified correctly among the 6 classes.

factors.name: method
factors.description: linear_svm: standardized LinearSVC with CV-tuned C (baseline). expand_sparsify: random sparse binary expansion + k-WTA + binary Hebbian readout (paper). rbf_svm: CV-tuned RBF SVM (optimised non-linear reference).

factors.name: mixture_nonlinearity
factors.description: Strength of sensor saturation and mixture interaction terms; 0 means purely additive mixtures.

factors.name: sensor_noise
factors.description: Std of additive per-sample sensor noise (plus baseline offset noise) relative to signal scale around 1.

factors.name: n_per_class
factors.description: Labelled training exposures per class (few-shot recalibration vs moderate data).
